reason: The text (Exodus 14) contains a clear passage where the Israelite people complain directly to Moses, their leader. After seeing the Egyptian forces pursuing them, they voice their complaint: 'Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you took us to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us to bring us out of Egypt?' (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה). They further express regret, saying they would have been better off remaining as slaves in Egypt rather than dying in the desert. This constitutes a clear complaint from the Hebrew people (bəne Yisrael) directed against their leader Moses.
